name: The University of Arizona

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in for 2025-26; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator). Reported intent to fund at/near full cap despite university budget crisis (not verified).

ratingNotes: FB: 10-3 in 2023 (Alamo Bowl win, Jedd Fisch), 4-8 in 2024 (Brent Brennan yr 1, first Big 12 season), 2025 rebound to a winning record and bowl (approx. 9-4, unverified). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Tommy Lloyd — #2 seed/Sweet 16 (2024), #4 seed/Sweet 16 loss to Duke (2025); 2025-26 a national-title contender ranked No. 1 for stretches with freshmen Koa Peat and Brayden Burries (NCAA result unverified). WBB: Adia Barnes left for SMU (2025); rebuilding. Olympic: historic top-25 Directors' Cup program (softball, swimming, golf, track); recent finishes roughly 30s-40s (approx.). Brand: basketball-led; football draws modestly. Facilities: aging Arizona Stadium; McKale is a top Big 12 hoops venue.
notes: University-wide financial crisis (FY2023-24 shortfall reported ~$177M+) led to Arizona Board of Regents oversight, repayment of internal loans to athletics (~$86M reported) and President Robert Robbins' exit; Suresh Garimella hired Oct 2024. Joined the Big 12 Aug 2024 with ASU, Colorado and Utah after the Pac-12 collapse. Basketball is the brand/political core (McKale sellouts); football revenue lags peers. Event hooks: athletics budget cuts, ABOR scrutiny of deficits, poaching interest in Lloyd.

name: Arizona State University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); expected to pay full cap (not verified).

ratingNotes: FB: Kenny Dillingham — 3-9 (2023, self-imposed bowl ban), 11-3 Big 12 champion in first season (2024) and CFP quarterfinal 2OT loss to Texas (Peach Bowl) with Cam Skattebo; 2025 dipped to roughly 8-5 amid QB Sam Leavitt's injury (approx.); Dillingham extended through 2030. 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Bobby Hurley — one NCAA win since 2019, 13-20 in 2024-25; job status after 2025-26 unverified. Olympic: wrestling, swimming (2024 NCAA men's swim title), golf, track — Directors' Cup roughly top-30. Facilities: renovated stadium, new Mullett Arena (hockey). Enrollment = campus-immersion headcount (~180k incl. online).

headMbbCoach.name: Bobby Hurley
headMbbCoach.note: Retained for 2025-26 after 13-20 season; status after March 2026 not verified.

notes: Michael Crow's ASU is an entrepreneurial, growth-at-all-costs actor (largest U.S. enrollment incl. online; AAU member since 2023). Phoenix (#12 DMA) is the Big 12's second-largest market after DFW/Houston. Football surge under Dillingham made ASU the more realignment-attractive Arizona school; NCAA penalties (2024) for Herm Edwards-era recruiting violations. Event hooks: Arizona Board of Regents dynamics with financially strained Arizona; Big Ten/SEC interest in Phoenix market.

name: Baylor University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); expected full cap (private school — figures are EADA-style estimates).

ratingNotes: FB: 2021 Big 12 champion (Sugar Bowl win); 3-9 (2023), 8-5 (2024, Texas Bowl), losing 2025 (~5-7, approx.) with Dave Aranda reportedly retained. 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Scott Drew — 2021 national champion; #3 seed (2024), #9 seed R2 loss to Duke (2025); 2025-26 midseason signing of ex-G League/draft pick James Nnaji drew national criticism. WBB: Nicki Collen, regular top-4/5 seed (3 titles under Kim Mulkey). Olympic: equestrian, acrobatics & tumbling, track, tennis — Directors' Cup roughly top-50. Facilities: McLane Stadium (2014), Foster Pavilion (2024).

headFootballCoach.name: Dave Aranda
headFootballCoach.note: Reported retained after 2025 losing season; verify for 2026.

notes: Private Baptist university. 2016 sexual-assault scandal (Art Briles, Ken Starr) and 2021 NCAA ruling with no major penalties. Texas politicians historically protected Baylor's seat (1994 SWC-to-Big 12 merger; 2010-11 Big 12 survival). Billionaire donors (Drayton McLane, Paul Foster) fund facilities. Smallest market of the Texas Big 12 schools; a 'protected by politics, not by market' realignment profile.
note: Football coach status for 2026 not verified.

name: Brigham Young University
religious: LDS (The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints)

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); expected full cap (church-owned; finances not fully public).

ratingNotes: FB: Kalani Sitake — 11-2 (2024, Alamo Bowl win over Colorado); 2025 11-1 regular season, lost Big 12 title game to Texas Tech and missed the CFP (approx. 12-2 final; bowl unverified); extended after Penn State interest (Nov 2025). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Kevin Young (ex-Phoenix Suns assistant) — #6 seed Sweet 16 (2025); landed No. 1 recruit AJ Dybantsa for 2025-26 (NCAA result unverified). Olympic: Directors' Cup No. 25 in 2024-25 (verified; cross country, track, volleyball). Fan base: national LDS following, top-tier attendance and travel.
notes: Owned by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints; no competition on Sundays (a scheduling constraint written into its Big 12 membership). FBS independent 2011-22 (ESPN deal), MWC before that; joined Big 12 2023 with phased-in shares. Holy War with Utah is a conference game again from 2024. Wealthy alumni (e.g., Utah Jazz owner Ryan Smith) and collectives support NIL; church leadership functions as the real board, so state political pressure is low.

name: University of Cincinnati

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); full-cap commitment reported but funding relies on university/donor support (not verified).

ratingNotes: FB: 2021 CFP semifinalist (first G5 playoff team, Luke Fickell); since Big 12 entry: 3-9 (2023), 5-7 (2024), bowl-eligible ~7-5 in 2025 after a strong start (approx.). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Wes Miller — NIT-level 2023-25, no NCAA bid since 2019; status after 2025-26 unverified. Olympic: Directors' Cup usually outside the top 75. Facilities: historic but small Nippert Stadium; renovated Fifth Third Arena.
notes: Former Big East (2005-13) and American (2013-23) member that earned Big 12 entry in 2023 with phased-in shares. Revenue gap vs. Big 12 peers, small stadium and an Ohio market dominated by Ohio State are recurring storylines; Crosstown Shootout with Xavier is a city institution. Ohio legislature (SB1 higher-ed law, 2025) shows willingness to legislate campus matters but little athletics intervention history.

name: University of Colorado Boulder

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); expected full cap.

ratingNotes: FB: Deion Sanders — 4-8 (2023), 9-4 (2024, Heisman winner Travis Hunter, Shedeur Sanders; Alamo Bowl loss to BYU), 3-9 (2025). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. Among the nation's most-watched teams 2023-24 ('Prime effect'). MBB: Tad Boyle — #10 seed R2 (2024), 14-21 (2024-25). WBB: JR Payne, Sweet 16s 2023-24. Olympic: skiing (multiple NCAA titles), cross country/track — Directors' Cup roughly top-60. Endowment is CU Foundation/system level.
notes: Left the Big 12 for the Pac-12 in 2011 and was the first Pac-12 school to jump back (announced July 2023, effective 2024). Coach Prime made CU a TV-ratings and NIL magnet; Sanders signed a five-year, ~$54M extension (Mar 2025) and had bladder-cancer surgery (2025). Elected CU Board of Regents; CU system president Todd Saliman; Colorado legislature rarely intervenes. Event hook: what happens to the brand if Sanders leaves.

name: University of Houston

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); expected full cap.

ratingNotes: FB: Willie Fritz — 4-8 (2024), rebound to ~9-3 plus bowl in 2025 with QB Conner Weigman (approx.). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Kelvin Sampson — #1 seed 2023, 2024, 2025; 2025 national runner-up (lost 65-63 to Florida); 2021 Final Four; Big 12 regular-season titles 2024 & 2025; 2025-26 again a top-seed contender (result unverified). Olympic: track & field tradition; Directors' Cup roughly top-80. Endowment = UH System.
notes: SWC member left out of the 1994 Big 12 merger; C-USA (1996-2013), American (2013-23), Big 12 since 2023. Tilman Fertitta (Rockets owner; longtime regents chair until becoming U.S. Ambassador to Italy in 2025) is the dominant booster. Texas legislature/governor care about keeping Texas schools in P4 after Texas/Texas A&M/OU left the Big 12 footprint. Sampson succession is a looming storyline.

name: Iowa State University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); full cap announced.

ratingNotes: FB: Matt Campbell era (2016-25) peaked at 11-3 in 2024 (Big 12 title game, Pop-Tarts Bowl win); ~8-4 in 2025 (opened with Dublin win over K-State). Otzelberger — #2 seed Sweet 16 (2024), #3 seed (2025), 2025-26 top-10 team (result unverified). WBB: Bill Fennelly, regular NCAA team (Audi Crooks). Olympic: wrestling, cross country, track — Directors' Cup roughly top-60. Fan base: 'Hilton Magic', strong attendance for market size.

headFootballCoach.name: Jimmy Rogers
headFootballCoach.note: Reported hire after Matt Campbell left for Penn State (Dec 2025).

notes: Governed with Iowa and Northern Iowa by the Iowa Board of Regents; the Cy-Hawk series with Iowa is a fixture legislators watch. Small Des Moines-Ames market but loyal fan base; a frequently cited 'left behind' school in the 2021-23 Big 12 crisis. Losing Campbell to a Big Ten school shows the P2 poaching coaches even when schools stay put.
note: New football coach and presidential status not web-verified.

name: The University of Kansas

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); expected full cap.

ratingNotes: FB: Lance Leipold revival — 9-4 (2023), 5-7 (2024, home games at Arrowhead during renovation), ~5-7 (2025, approx.). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Bill Self — 2008 & 2022 national titles, record Big 12 regular-season titles; preseason No. 1 in 2024-25 but #7 seed R1 loss to Arkansas (2025); 2025-26 featured projected top NBA pick Darryn Peterson (result unverified). WBB: Brandon Schneider, bubble. Olympic: track, rowing — Directors' Cup roughly top-70. Facilities: Gateway District rebuild of the stadium (capacity approx. post-renovation).
notes: Basketball blue blood; Self on a 'lifetime' rolling contract; the NCAA IARP infractions case closed in 2023 without a postseason ban. $450M-plus Gateway District project (David Booth donor) rebuilt the stadium. Kansas Board of Regents and legislature (STAR bonds, Chiefs/Royals stadium politics) treat KU and K-State as a pair; KU is a perennial Big Ten/ACC realignment name because of basketball + AAU status.

name: Texas Tech University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); pays full cap and supplements via Matador Club/Campbell-backed NIL — among the nation's largest roster budgets.

ratingNotes: FB: Joey McGuire — 8-5 (2024); 2025 Big 12 champion (beat BYU in title game), CFP first-round bye, quarterfinal loss (approx. 12-2) with an NIL-built roster (reported $25M+ for football). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Grant McCasland — #3 seed Elite Eight (2025, JT Toppin). Softball: NiJaree Canady ($1M+ NIL) led 2025 WCWS final run. Olympic: track & field, golf, baseball — Directors' Cup roughly top-35. Facilities: new south end zone complex (2024).
notes: Board of Regents chair Cody Campbell (energy billionaire) and the Matador Club drive an all-in strategy; Campbell is also a national voice on federal college-sports legislation and the 2025 'Saving College Sports' push. TTU System chancellor Brandon Creighton (former state senator, 2025) links the program to Austin. Remote Lubbock market but huge West Texas following; Texas legislature historically intervenes (1994, 2010).

name: University of Central Florida

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); full cap reported (not verified).

ratingNotes: FB: claimed 2017 national title (13-0), 2018 NY6; Big 12 years: 6-7 (2023), 4-8 (2024, Gus Malzahn left), ~5-7 (2025, Scott Frost's return, approx.). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Johnny Dawkins — NIT/CBI level. Olympic: Directors' Cup roughly top-90. Facilities: modest on-campus stadium; newer football operations building.
notes: One of the largest U.S. universities by enrollment, in the fast-growing Orlando DMA — the Big 12's Florida/market play (joined 2023). Florida Board of Governors and DeSantis-appointed trustees mean high state pressure; War on I-4 with USF paused since UCF left the American. Endowment is small relative to enrollment.

name: The University of Utah

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); full cap, with the Otro Capital partnership (2025) aimed at funding growth.

ratingNotes: FB: Pac-12 champions 2021 & 2022 (Rose Bowls); 5-7 (2024, first Big 12 year); ~10-2 plus bowl (2025, approx.). Kyle Whittingham stepped down after 2025 (reported hired by Michigan, verify); coach-in-waiting Morgan Scalley promoted. 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Craig Smith fired 2025; Alex Jensen (NBA assistant, Utah alum) hired. WBB: Lynne Roberts left for the WNBA (late 2024); Gavin Petersen. Olympic: gymnastics (perennial NCAA contender), skiing (multiple recent NCAA titles) — Directors' Cup roughly top-45.
notes: First Power-conference athletic department to bring in private equity: a for-profit 'Utah Brands & Entertainment' entity with a minority investment from Otro Capital (announced late 2025; university retains control) — a template for Big 12 peers and the conference's own private-capital talks. Gov. Spencer Cox publicly backed the 2023 Big 12 move. Holy War with BYU now a league game.
note: Football coach transition and PE deal terms not web-verified.

name: West Virginia University

athletics.revShareNotes: Opted in; House settlement cap $20.5M in 2025-26 (≈$21.3M in 2026-27 after 4% escalator); full cap pledged (not verified) despite university budget strain.

ratingNotes: FB: Neal Brown fired after 6-7 (2024); Rich Rodriguez returned for 2025 — rebuilding year (~4-8, approx.). 2026 season-to-date results not verified for this snapshot. MBB: Darian DeVries one season (19-13, NCAA snub in 2025) then left for Indiana; Ross Hodge (North Texas) hired. WBB: Mark Kellogg, NCAA 2023-25. Olympic: rifle dynasty (~20 NCAA titles) — Directors' Cup roughly top-90. Fan base: statewide flagship following; Morgantown lies in the Clarksburg-Weston DMA (Pittsburgh spillover).
notes: Geographic outlier (nearest Big 12 peer Cincinnati ~270 miles straight-line; most are 800+); joined 2012 when the Big East fractured. 2023 academic restructuring under Gordon Gee (dozens of programs cut amid a ~$45M deficit) shows financial strain; Michael Benson succeeded Gee Jan 2025. Gov. Patrick Morrisey and Sen. Jim Justice are vocal about WVU; Backyard Brawl with Pitt resumed 2022-25. Below-average Big 12 revenue vs. travel costs is a recurring 'should WVU look east?' storyline.
